{"decision":"Standup meeting record — agreed_angle.md
Date: Thursday, 10 September 2026
Chair: Boss Dave
Attendees: Alice (Search, RAG & Market Discovery), Eve (Markdown Reports & Interface Builder), Bob (Database Queries & File Management)
Reference: research_summary.md (Alice) — reviewed at meeting.

1) Chosen angle (consensus)
We will produce a concise, practical comparative report titled: "From Lab to Land: Translating PV efficiency records into real‑world yield and procurement guidance." The report will focus on bridging lab-record efficiencies and everyday, project-level energy yield projections and procurement decisions. It will emphasize reproducible data sources, measurement context (STC/NOCT/cell vs module vs system), and actionable derating/selection guidance for practitioners.

Rationale: This angle leverages the existing research_summary.md content (which already contrasts lab vs commercial/module/system performance and lists sources) and addresses the user need for a report that is directly useful to project developers, energy modelers, and procurement/policy analysts.

2) Target audience (consensus)
Primary: Solar project developers, procurement leads, energy modelers/analysts, technical policy advisors — readers with technical aptitude who need practical, reproducible guidance to convert efficiency numbers into expected field yield and procurement choices.
Secondary: Informed industry analysts and advanced students wanting a compact, source‑linked technical overview.

Tone/technical level: Concise, technically precise but pragmatic — assume readers understand basic PV terminology but require clear definitions and reproducible data links (not introductory lay explanations).

3) Agreed 3‑section outline
Section 1 — Key metrics, context & quick reference (approx. 10% of report)
- Clear definitions: STC, NOCT, aperture area vs active area, nameplate vs measured output, cell vs module vs system efficiencies, and standard test conditions vs field conditions.
- Quick-reference table: mapping common efficiency numbers (lab cell record / certified cell / typical module / premium module / system yield factors) to the measurement context and typical uncertainty/degradation ranges.
- Short note on sources & reproducibility expectations (how we report dataset version/access date).

Section 2 — Comparative performance and loss factors (approx. 55% of report)
- Side‑by‑side presentation: lab record efficiencies (certified research-cell) vs commercial module efficiencies vs typical system-level yield (kWh/kWp/year) across representative technologies (mono‑c‑Si, multi‑c‑Si, thin‑film, perovskite/tandem where relevant).
- Quantify typical gaps and causes: optical losses, temperature and NOCT effects, soiling, mismatch, inverter losses, shading/tilt/azimuth, degradation rates — present typical derating percentages and ranges with provenance.
- Short examples (one residential, one utility-scale) that convert module efficiency into estimated annual yield using common climates (temperate, hot/dry, high latitude).

Section 3 — Practical recommendations, data provenance & procurement implications (approx. 35% of report)
- Practical rules of thumb for procurement and modeling (e.g., how to translate manufacturer module efficiency into expected site kWh/kWp/year and how to choose derating factors based on environment and mounting).
- Data and reproducibility checklist: mandated citation formats, dataset versions, snapshot practice, example scripts for reproducible weighting/aggregation.
- Policy/market implications & next steps: where improved reporting or standardized metadata would most reduce uncertainty for deployers.

4) Follow‑up data tasks & assignments (agreed, with deliverables and due dates)
- Alice: Correct the misnamed NREL citation in research_summary.md (replace the "National Laboratory of the Rockies" entry with the correct NREL Best Research‑Cell Efficiency Chart citation and URL), record dataset version and access date, and verify that any mirror link truly reproduces the same data. Deliverable: updated bibliography entry + brief provenance note (filename: research_summary_references.md). Due: EOD Monday 14 Sep 2026.
  - Rationale/agreement: We agree with Alice that the citation is incorrect and must be corrected. No disagreement.

- Eve: Add the compact "metrics & context" box into the report (definitions for STC/NOCT/aperture vs active area; clear cell/module/system distinctions) and produce a 1‑slide bulleted standup summary derived from the report. Deliverables: updated report draft section 1 (file: section1_metrics_context.md) and slide bullet file (section1_slide.txt). Due: EOD Monday 14 Sep 2026.
  - Rationale/agreement: We agree with Eve that measurement conditions must be explicit to avoid misinterpretation. No disagreement.

- Bob: Attach the exact Fraunhofer dataset/URL/DOI with retrieval date and provide a reproducible snapshot (CSV or JSON) plus a short script/notebook showing the weighting calculation used to derive the quoted 22–23% weighted average for c‑Si modules. Deliverables: fraunhofer_snapshot.csv (or .json), weighting_script.ipynb (or .py), and a provenance note (fraunhofer_provenance.md). Due: EOD Monday 14 Sep 2026.
  - Partial clarification/disagreement: We agree with Bob that the Fraunhofer weighted average must be reproducible. However, we prefer that large data snapshots be stored in the team’s central data repo with a link from the report rather than embedding large files in the markdown report itself. Bob should therefore place the snapshot and script in the central repo and include a short retrieval/verification note in the research_summary revisions. (This is a process preference, not a rejection of Bob’s request.)

- Coordination task (Boss Dave / Alice & Bob): Produce a short authoritative dataset list (NREL chart, Fraunhofer ISE PV module/market survey, IEA‑PVPS 2025/2026 reports, representative manufacturer datasheets) with preferred citation format and access dates. Deliverable: datasets_list.md. Due: Wednesday 16 Sep 2026.

5) Next steps & meeting cadence
- Immediate: Assigned persons update the research_summary.md and the supporting files listed above by EOD Mon 14 Sep 2026.
- Quick sync: 30‑minute check‑in on Wednesday 16 Sep 2026 to review updated materials and finalize the 3‑section draft for internal review.

6) Decision log and where we disagreed
- All core requested corrections (Alice, Eve, Bob) were accepted and assigned. The only divergence is procedural: Bob’s original instruction to "attach" dataset snapshots directly to the summary is modified — we ask him to store snapshots and scripts in the central data repo and link them from the report for version control and size management. The team agreed this change.

Recorded by: Boss Dave (chair)
","title":"agreed_angle.md"}
